content.user_title: Analyze WebAsk Survey Comments by Theme
content.value_statement: Open survey responses are difficult to compare as long lists of comments. This skill organizes WebAsk responses into themes with counts, percentages, and representative quotes.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve text responses for one survey question with get_quiz_report_inputs, using get_quiz_report first when filtering is needed.
Group responses by meaning and rank themes by response counts and percentages.
Count empty or non-substantive responses separately without hiding their frequency.
Select representative verbatim quotes while removing personal information.
Note sentiment when it is discernible and identify two or three recurring themes for action.
Respond in the user language and acknowledge sparse or unstructured evidence.
limitations: Requires access to the WebAsk MCP reporting tools; the skill does not provide their server implementation.
Analyzes each open question separately and does not combine different questions into one theme analysis.
Small samples and unrelated responses may not support reliable conclusions or meaningful themes.
Stops when service limits prevent progress and does not recommend upgrades or direct users to payment.

use_cases.title: Prioritize customer experience issues
use_cases.description: Rank recurring service complaints by frequency and review representative quotes before choosing improvements.

use_cases.title: Review product improvement requests
use_cases.description: Group answers to a product improvement question by meaning and distinguish repeated requests from isolated comments.

use_cases.title: Summarize a survey subgroup
use_cases.description: Filter a survey report, analyze the selected text responses, and report theme frequencies with sample limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize one question
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the open responses to [question] in WebAsk survey [survey]. Show the most common themes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain a first thematic summary.

prompt_templates.title: Add counts and quotes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [question] in survey [survey]. Rank themes by count and percentage, include representative quotes, and count non-substantive answers separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an evidence-based response summary.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a filtered group
prompt_templates.prompt: Filter survey [survey] by [condition], then analyze [question] for that group. Include counts, percentages, sentiment where clear, and quotes without personal data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: understand feedback from a defined respondent group.

prompt_templates.title: Review several questions separately
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [questions] in survey [survey] separately. For each, report ranked themes, counts, percentages, redacted quotes, and sample limitations. Identify two or three recurring priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce separate summaries without mixing answers across questions.

output_examples.input: Illustrative responses: 'Long wait', 'Waited forty minutes', 'Price was unclear', and '-'. Group them by theme.
output: Waiting time: 2 of 4 responses, 50%. Representative quote: 'Waited forty minutes'.
Price clarity: 1 of 4 responses, 25%. Representative quote: 'Price was unclear'.
This sample is too small for firm conclusions. Waiting time and price clarity are preliminary areas to investigate.

output_examples.input: Illustrative responses: 'Helpful staff', 'Staff were rude', and 'Helpful and patient staff'. Summarize themes and sentiment.
output: Sentiment is mixed: two positive responses and one negative response.
Representative quotes: 'Helpful and patient staff' and 'Staff were rude'.
The sample is too small for general conclusions. Positive comments do not erase the negative experience.

best_practices: Specify the survey, question, and any filter before requesting analysis.
Review theme counts alongside representative quotes and the number of non-substantive responses.
Check quote redactions and sample limitations before sharing a report.
anti_patterns: Combining responses from different questions into one thematic summary.
Demanding a preferred conclusion when the responses support different themes.
Publishing identifiable quotes or treating a few responses as conclusive evidence.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill require?
faq.answer: It depends on the WebAsk MCP tools get_quiz_report and get_quiz_report_inputs.

faq.question: Can it analyze a filtered group?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow first uses get_quiz_report with a filter, then analyzes text responses for the selected group.

faq.question: How are themes formed?
faq.answer: Responses are grouped by meaning rather than exact wording. Each theme includes a count, percentage, and representative quote.

faq.question: How does it handle empty answers?
faq.answer: Empty and non-substantive answers form a separate counted group. They are not hidden or treated as substantive themes.

faq.question: Are quotes copied exactly?
faq.answer: The instructions preserve original wording and typos, but require personal information such as names and phone numbers to be removed.

faq.question: What happens when there is too little data?
faq.answer: The skill states that the sample is small and avoids firm conclusions. It also acknowledges when responses do not form meaningful themes.
